concepts.title: Economic Activities and Definition of a Worker

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Economic Activities and Definition of a Worker' refers to.
questions.a: An economic activity encompasses all actions contributing to national product, and any individual engaged in such productive efforts—whether self-employed, hired, or temporarily absent due to illness—is classified as a worker.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Economic Activities and Definition of a Worker'.
questions.a: Every individual contributing directly or through assisting roles to the production of goods and services is part of the workforce.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Economic Activities and Definition of a Worker', in plain ASCII form.

Calculate the worker-population ratio. Use the method 'Worker-Population Ratio'. Work with: ratio = 60, total_population = 2500, total_workers = 12000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.

Find the worker-population ratio given total workers and population. Use the method 'Worker-Population Ratio'. Work with: ratio = 80, total_population = 48000, total_workers = 48000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
Explain in your own words what 'Worker-Population Ratio' refers to.
questions.a: The worker-population ratio measures the proportion of a country's total population that actively participates in the production of goods and services.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Worker-Population Ratio'.
questions.a: A higher worker-population ratio indicates greater engagement of the population in economic activities.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Worker-Population Ratio', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio

questions.q: Find the number of workers given population and WPR. Use the method 'Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio'. Work with: population = 5000, total_product = 6, worker_population_ratio = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.

Calculate the estimated number of workers in urban area. Use the method 'Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio'. Work with: population = 125000, total_product = 5, worker_population_ratio = 125000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
Explain in your own words what 'Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio' refers to.
questions.a: The total workforce in a given region or country can be calculated by applying the worker-population ratio to the aggregate population.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio'.
questions.a: Total number of employed persons equals the product of population and participation rate divided by 100.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Estimation of Workforce from Worker-Population Ratio', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Classification of Workers by Employment Status

questions.q: Using the method 'Classification of Workers by Employment Status', work with: casual_wage_labourers = 1000, regular_salaried = 20, self_employed = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_workforce.

Take the relation taught for 'Classification of Workers by Employment Status' and work with: casual_wage_labourers = 1500, regular_salaried = 24, self_employed = 3. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_workforce.
Explain in your own words what 'Classification of Workers by Employment Status' refers to.
questions.a: Workers are grouped into self-employed individuals who operate their own enterprise, regular salaried employees who receive periodic wages with job continuity, and casual wage labourers hired intermittently without job security.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Classification of Workers by Employment Status'.
questions.a: Employment status reflects the nature of contractual arrangement, level of security, and authority over production.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Classification of Workers by Employment Status', in plain ASCII form.

Using the method 'Sectoral Distribution of Workforce', work with: primary_share = 0.45, secondary_share = 0.8, tertiary_share = 0.5. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_share.

Take the relation taught for 'Sectoral Distribution of Workforce' and work with: primary_share = 0.2, secondary_share = 0.2, tertiary_share = 0.4. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_share.
Explain in your own words what 'Sectoral Distribution of Workforce' refers to.
questions.a: Workforce allocation across primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction, utilities), and tertiary (services, trade, transport) sectors reflects economic structural composition.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Sectoral Distribution of Workforce'.
questions.a: Economic development traditionally drives structural shifts from primary agriculture to secondary manufacturing and tertiary service sectors.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Sectoral Distribution of Workforce', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce

questions.q: Using the method 'Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce', work with: employment_growth_rate = 20, gdp_growth_rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of employment_elasticity_of_growth.

Take the relation taught for 'Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce' and work with: employment_growth_rate = 25, gdp_growth_rate = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of employment_elasticity_of_growth.
Explain in your own words what 'Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce' refers to.
questions.a: Jobless growth is a macroeconomic state where GDP expands without generating proportional employment opportunities, whereas casualisation refers to the structural drift of labour toward temporary casual wage work.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce'.
questions.a: Output expansion through capital-intensive methods fails to absorb labour, pushing displaced workers into unprotected casual jobs.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Jobless Growth and Casualisation of Workforce', in plain ASCII form.

Using the method 'Informalisation of the Workforce', work with: fraction = 0.75, informal_workers = 12000, total_workers = 48000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.

Take the relation taught for 'Informalisation of the Workforce' and work with: fraction = 0.6, informal_workers = 2500, total_workers = 1200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of the result.
Explain in your own words what 'Informalisation of the Workforce' refers to.
questions.a: Formal sector units comprise public enterprises and private establishments with 10 or more hired workers providing social security, while informal units comprise all remaining small enterprises, self-employed, and casual laborers lacking social protection.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Informalisation of the Workforce'.
questions.a: The informal sector lacks labour legislation protections, social security benefits, and trade union representation.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Informalisation of the Workforce', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal

questions.q: Using the method 'Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal', work with: labour_force = 80, workforce = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of unemployed_count.

Take the relation taught for 'Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal' and work with: labour_force = 75, workforce = 25. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of unemployed_count.
Explain in your own words what 'Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal' refers to.
questions.a: Unemployment occurs when individuals willing and able to work at prevailing wages cannot find work; it manifests as open unemployment, disguised unemployment (marginal productivity of surplus labour is zero), or seasonal unemployment (lack of year-round agricultural work).

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal'.
questions.a: Disguised unemployment conceals excess labour in farming where removing workers does not diminish total output.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Forms of Unemployment: Open, Disguised, and Seasonal', in plain ASCII form.

concepts.title: Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation

questions.q: Using the method 'Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation', work with: direct_employment = 8, indirect_employment = 300. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_employment_generated.

Take the relation taught for 'Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation' and work with: direct_employment = 50, indirect_employment = 18. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of total_employment_generated.
Explain in your own words what 'Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation' refers to.
questions.a: The government generates employment directly by hiring staff in public departments and state-owned enterprises, and indirectly through multiplier effects when increased public sector output stimulates demand in supplying and purchasing private industries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation'.
questions.a: Public enterprise expansion and statutory schemes like MGNREGA provide both direct livelihood and stimulate indirect private sector employment.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Government Direct and Indirect Employment Generation', in plain ASCII form.
